investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing via Shared ELB Dependency
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-30T01:02–01:03Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway at the AWS ELB endpoint (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents). Because every check shares the same error message and the failure occurs before any agent identity or VM state is returned, the swarm gateway or its ELB is the earliest violated dependency, not any individual check's logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — fronted by an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agent check calls POST /api/agents as its first step, which in turn proxies to http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents. That upstream request failed with a network-level error ("error sending request for url"), causing the production-api to return HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" before any agent provisioning could begin. No evidence of a user-traffic incident or production outage is present in the packet; this is an eval-detected infrastructure availability signal localized to the swarm gateway / ELB layer.

Lower probability: A DNS resolution failure for the ELB hostname caused the 'error sending request for url' message, though the URL being fully formed in the error suggests DNS resolved but the TCP/HTTP connection failed.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — fronted by an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. That upstream request failed with a network-level error ("error sending request for url"), causing the production-api to return HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" before any agent provisioning could begin. No evidence of a user-traffic incident or production outage is present in the packet; this is an eval-detected infrastructure availability signal localized to the swarm gateway / ELB layer.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-08-30T01:03 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the POST /api/agents provisioning step — before any agent identity, model, or runtime response can be returned — every required evidence field (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is absent and the expected-output contract is fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" on POST /api/agents for every remote-agent check. Because agent provisioning is the first step in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918: createAgent(..., "remote", ...)), no downstream evidence — orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message — could be collected, causing a complete contract gap across all three sibling checks. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB (us-east-2) was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — strongest evidence, directly stated in the 502 error body across all three checks.
Transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api layer and the swarm gateway ELB, causing connection errors on all outbound requests to /v1/agents.
Swarm gateway deployment or scaling event in progress at ~01:03 UTC on 2026-08-30 that temporarily removed all healthy ELB targets.
Security group, VPC routing, or load-balancer listener misconfiguration introduced around the time of the eval run that blocked traffic to the ELB.

Eval runner credential or endpoint configuration issue causing requests to be routed to an incorrect or decommissioned ELB address — less likely given the error explicitly names the ELB and the gateway error message is application-level.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=748, max=300)
investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 748 minutes old, exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot publication pipeline rather than the public web surface itself.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 748 minutes (~12.5 hours). The snapshot file is reachable and structurally valid (all required evidence fields are present, source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true), but its embedded generation timestamp is stale beyond the 300-minute contract threshold defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482). This is an eval-detected staleness condition in the snapshot publication pipeline; no evidence of a user-facing page outage is present.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 748' — the sole violated assertion, confirmed by the check message and raw evidence (failed-check.evidence).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=748, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot is structurally intact and claims a live GitHub Actions source, but the age value alone breaches the contract.
expected-output.contract: infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 asserts { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 }; the observed value of 748 directly violates this assertion.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed (status=200, hasAppShell=true, allRoutesOk=true), including the /observability route itself — confirming the public website is reachable and the failure is isolated to the snapshot content pipeline.
source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: the check is registered as required=false, statusImpact=informational — this is an informational eval failure, not a required check outage.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from statusSnapshotEvidence(payload), confirming the age is computed from the live snapshot content at eval time.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot has not triggered or completed successfully in over 748 minutes. This could be due to a workflow schedule gap, a cancelled/skipped run, a workflow failure that did not re-publish the file, or a GitHub Actions quota/runner availability issue.

Less likely but plausible: The workflow ran but failed to write or push the updated status.json to the GitHub Pages branch, leaving the previously published stale file in place. The snapshot's source field still reads 'github-actions' because it reflects the last successful write, not the most recent run attempt.

Least likely: The snapshotAgeMinutes computation in statusSnapshotEvidence() is incorrect (e.g., clock skew or timestamp parsing error), causing an inflated age reading despite a recent actual publication. This is unlikely given the magnitude of the discrepancy (748 vs. 300 minutes).
